parent_models.justification: Partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA) is an extension of partial least squares regression, adapted for classification tasks. Both models use the PLS algorithm, but PLS-DA is tailored for categorical outcomes.

closest_parent_model.justification: PLS-DA is an adaptation of partial least squares regression specifically for classification tasks, making PLS regression the closest parent model in terms of methodology and foundational algorithm.

closest_child_model.justification: There are no specific child models listed that are more specialized or subclass models of partial least-squares discriminant analysis.

sibling_models.justification: Partial least squares correlation is a concept related to the partial least squares methodology, often used alongside regression and discriminant analysis, making it a sibling model.

closest_sibling_model.justification: Among the siblings, partial least squares correlation shares the most similarity with partial least-squares discriminant analysis in terms of applying PLS in different scenarios, specifically focusing on correlation.
